channel.title: X-Autopilot
channel.description: Auto-update feed for X-Autopilot Mac app

item.title: v2.0.16
item.description:
### Payment provider: Dodo Payments
X-Autopilot now bills through Dodo Payments instead of Lemon Squeezy (both are Merchants of Record — they handle global tax/VAT). A behind-the-scenes switch; nothing about how you use the app changes.
The in-app activation screen and billing panel now reference Dodo Payments (your license key arrives in a Dodo receipt email after purchase). New website purchases go through Dodo checkout.
Your existing license keeps working. Pricing is identical (Starter $19/mo, Pro $39/mo, Lifetime $199). Auto-update via the in-app updater.

item.title: v2.0.15
item.description:
### Fix morning-session crash loop
Some users saw the agent rapidly cycle through short sessions ("stuck in a loop") doing little work.
Cause: when a morning session generated its daily deep-dive thread, it picked a topic from your Content Topics list. If that list was empty (the default on a fresh install), the pick crashed, which killed the whole session before it did real work. Because the crash happened before the "thread done today" marker was written, the next session retried the same crash, over and over. Afternoon and evening sessions were never affected.
Fixes: empty Content Topics now falls back to defaults instead of crashing; thread generation is isolated so a failure is logged and skipped while the session continues with replies/likes/follows; and a noisy token-refresh log race from v2.0.12 is fixed.
Tip: set Content Topics in Settings for the best threads, but you no longer need to for the agent to run safely.
Auto-update via the in-app updater (within 24h).

item.title: v2.0.14
item.description:
### Product replies always link your domain
The product-mention promotions feature now reliably includes your product's domain (e.g. ampliflow.in, xautopilot.app) in every reply.
Previously the prompt asked the AI to include the URL but it occasionally dropped it when the value-add ran long. Now it's deterministic: the agent gets the bare domain, is told to include it as a non-negotiable rule in plain text, and a post-generation guarantee check appends it if missing (or normalizes a full https:// form to the clean bare domain). 100% of product replies now carry your domain, written like a builder casually sharing their work.
Unchanged: the 4/day product-reply cap, keyword matching, and value-first behavior.
Auto-update via the in-app updater (within 24h).

item.title: v2.0.13
item.description: ### Voice profile generation starts immediately Fixes the most-reported Voice Lab issue: clicking "Generate Voice Profile" while the agent was mid-session left you staring at "waiting for agent…" for many minutes. ### What was wrong The voice generator shares the agent's browser, so it was only checked BETWEEN sessions. But a turbo/aggressive session runs 15-35 minutes. A mid-session click sat in the queue until the whole session finished — one reported case waited 35 minutes (queued 11:07, started 11:42). ### The fix The agent now checks for a pending voice request between every action and during between-session sleeps, so a mid-session click is served within seconds of the current action completing. The check is a single file-existence test — zero cost when nothing is queued. The "waiting for agent…" message is also clearer now: it tells you the agent is finishing its current action and shows how long it's been queued, instead of looking frozen. ### Unchanged Generation quality, the 4-source builder (your tweets + reference accounts + self-description + fine-tune), pacing, daily caps — all identical. Pure responsiveness fix. ### Upgrade Auto-update via the in-app updater (within 24h on existing installs).

item.title: v2.0.12
item.description:
### Fix: "every relaunch asks me for my license key" Multiple buyers reported that closing and reopening the app dropped them back on the activation screen — even after correctly activating their license. Confirmed root cause, fixed end-to-end. ### The bug The cloud's subscription tokens had a 12-hour TTL but no refresh mechanism. After 12 hours every paid buyer hit a 401 on their next license check → the Mac eagerly cleared the local token → activation screen on the next launch. Repeat indefinitely. ### Cloud-side (helps all earlier versions immediately)
  • Token TTL: 12 hours → 90 days. Every existing buyer's token now lasts 3 months instead of half a day. The "every relaunch" loop is broken for everyone, including v2.0.10 and v2.0.11 users, without needing this update.
  • /v1/auth/me returns a refreshed subscription_token in every response.
### Mac-side (v2.0.12)
  • Auto-save the refreshed token. The dashboard polls cloud status every 5 seconds while open; v2.0.12 saves the rolling refreshed token from each response. Net effect: the token is essentially immortal while the app is in regular use.
  • Stop nuking the token on a single 401. Old behaviour was eager — one 401 wiped the local token, even if it was a transient cloud blip or clock skew. v2.0.12 logs the 401 and retries on the next call. Genuine subscription cancellation comes through as 402 (PaymentRequired), not 401, and that path still hard-blocks correctly.
### Net behaviour Before: paid buyer activates → 12hr later, every relaunch shows "Paste your license key". After: activate once, app remembers indefinitely. Activation screen only appears for fresh installs, explicit SIGN OUT, or cancelled subscriptions. ### Upgrade Auto-update via the in-app updater (within 24h on existing installs).

item.title: v2.0.11
item.description:
### Bot-fingerprint hardening — five layers fixed Buyers were reporting X showing the "we think you're automated" banner mid-session, which auto-pauses the agent. This release closes the deepest bot-detection signals identified by a systematic audit.
  • URL bot-signals dropped — search URLs no longer leak min_faves:50 operator or src=typed_query. Hashtag searches route through /hashtag/<topic> (mimics clicking a hashtag in a tweet). Engagement filtering moved client-side.
  • Action-type-aware delays — before, every gap between actions was uniform 60-180s regardless of action type. Now replies wait 120-600s, likes 20-80s, follows 15-60s. Plus 5-10% chance per action of taking a 5-20min "rabbit hole" dwell.
  • 47 openers, sliding-window dedup — was 16 openers with a soft cap. New list has 47, with strict "no non-empty opener may repeat within last 20 replies". Empties still ~25-30% to match casual-Twitter no-opener norms.
  • Multi-zone click offsets — clicks no longer always near centre (a known Puppeteer fingerprint). New distribution: 40% centre, 25% upper-left, 15% lower-right, 10% broad scatter, 10% edge-clip.
  • Variable typing speed by character class — uniform 20-70ms per keystroke replaced with per-class ranges (space 60-220ms thinking pause, common consonants 10-40ms, end-of-sentence 80-200ms, capitals get shift-key penalty). Plus 10% chance per word boundary of "burst mode": next 4-10 chars at 3× speed.
### What stays the same Daily caps, schedule, action types, all UI — zero functional changes. Pure stealth + reliability upgrade. ### Upgrade Auto-update via the in-app updater (within 24h on existing installs).

item.title: v2.0.10
item.description:
### Auto-respawn when Chrome dies If the agent's Chrome instance gets killed for any reason — you closed the window by reflex, the Mac slept and the WebSocket dropped, Chrome itself crashed — the agent now relaunches itself within a couple seconds. Before this release, it logged "Browser connection lost" and just exited, leaving buyers to find a dead agent in the morning after an overnight run. Pre-restart it kills any chrome_profile-locked process and clears Singleton lock files (same prep run_forever.sh does), so the new instance launches cleanly without a "Chrome is already running" wall. ### Guardrails Not an unbounded restart loop:
  • Only auto-respawns in the installed .app. Dev runs are unchanged.
  • Skips the respawn if you clicked QUIT in the dashboard — we don't fight a user who wanted out.
  • If 3+ respawns happen in any 5-minute window, the agent gives up. Something is fundamentally broken at that point and an unbounded loop would just burn battery. Manual relaunch resets the counter.
### What persists across the respawn Everything that matters: Twitter cookies, license token, voice profile, action history, today's counters. The respawn happens at the .app process level — ~/Library/Application Support/X-Autopilot/data/ is untouched. ### Upgrade path Auto-update via agent/updater.py. Existing v2.0.6 through v2.0.9 installs see the v2.0.10 banner on their next updater check (within 24h). DMG signature stapled — first launch is instant.

item.title: v2.0.9
item.description:
### In-app voice profile builder — no more copy-pasting tweets Old: copy a long prompt → open Claude.ai → paste 50–100 of your own tweets → copy result → paste back. ~20 minutes per setup. New: open the Voice tab, click GENERATE. Mix any of four sources:
  • Your tweets — auto-scraped from your X timeline via the agent's existing logged-in Chrome (or paste, or skip)
  • Reference accounts — up to 5 handles whose style you want to dial toward (@rauchg @paulg @swyx). The agent extracts patterns, not content.
  • Describe yourself — plain English. Highest-priority signal.
  • Fine-tune — anti-patterns, signature topics, length preference
Strict priority hierarchy in the prompt (description > constraints > references > own tweets) so the LLM doesn't mash sources together. ~60–90s, costs ~$0.01–0.05 on your configured LLM key. Preview + edit before save. Old external-LLM path preserved behind an "Advanced" disclosure for users who'd rather not burn their in-app tokens on a one-time setup. ### Dashboard auto-opens on first launch If you ever saw "icon keeps jumping in the dock but the app doesn't open" — this is the fix. The agent was running fine on localhost:5001 but never opened a browser window. Now it auto-opens the dashboard when onboarding is needed, when the subscription state is inactive, or when a duplicate launch detects the existing instance. ### UI cleanup across the dashboard
  • Blank-page on fresh install fixed — rules-of-hooks violation in SubscriptionGate was tearing down the React tree on every first launch.
  • Activation celebration — license-key accepted now shows a glowing "You're on Lifetime" screen with tier perks instead of silently flipping into the dashboard.
  • AI Provider step has room to breathe — option cards widened from 160px to 230px, hints in mixed case with proper line-height, RECOMMENDED badge moved above the name.
  • Lifetime billing button stopped going nowhere — Lemon Squeezy doesn't provision a customer-portal URL for one-time orders. MANAGE BILLING is hidden for Lifetime/Founder; replaced with a one-line caption explaining the receipt is in their email.
  • Duplicate SUBSCRIPTION panel removed — Settings tab was rendering a second subscription block under the LLM keys form.
  • Trial users see sharper copy at 100% quota — "Upgrade to Pro or Starter to continue, or add your own LLM key" instead of the misleading "wait until next month".
### DMG installer cleanup
  • Dropped Open My Chrome.command — dev leftover that looked like a random text file to buyers.
  • Fixed a long-standing create-dmg silent crash (pre-created Applications symlink collided with --app-drop-link), so the DMG layout is now the proper styled two-icon installer instead of the ugly hdiutil default.
### Cloud-side (deployed earlier) tier='lifetime' Postgres enum value added (every Lifetime activation was crashing without it). /v1/customer/portal-url returns clean 404 with a helpful message for one-time orders instead of confusing 502. ### Upgrade path Auto-update via agent/updater.py. Existing v2.0.6 / v2.0.7 / v2.0.8 installs see the v2.0.9 banner on their next updater check (within 24h). DMG signature stapled — first launch is instant, no Gatekeeper bouncing.

item.title: v2.0.8
item.description: ### Settings → License panel for Pro and Starter buyers Open Settings and you now see your subscription state right at the top. Tier (Lifetime / Pro / Starter), the email your account is bound to, and a colour-coded status badge — ACTIVE, TRIAL, PAYMENT FAILED, ENDING SOON, ACCESS REVOKED, TRIAL ENDED. For Pro and Starter, the panel also shows your monthly LLM token meter (usage / cap, with a coloured bar that turns yellow at 80% and red at 95%). Lifetime users don't see the meter — that tier is BYOK so usage is unlimited from the app's perspective. ### Manage billing without leaving the app Two new actions on the panel: - **MANAGE BILLING** opens the Lemon Squeezy customer portal in a new tab. Cancel, update card, change plan. Only renders if your tier has a payment account. - **SIGN OUT** clears your local subscription token, freeing this Mac as an activation slot. Useful when moving to a new machine. Comes with a confirm dialog that makes the distinction with "cancel subscription" explicit — signing out doesn't cancel. ### Period dates surface inline The panel shows what's actually scheduled: when the trial ends, when the next renewal hits, or — if you've cancelled — when access ends and the grace period closes. past_due gets a "Last payment failed" warning prompting you to open the portal. ### Why now Before v2.0.8, Pro and Starter buyers had no in-app way to check their state, see their token usage, or get to the billing portal. The only path was searching their inbox for the original Lemon Squeezy email. This panel makes all of it one click. ### What's unchanged No backend changes — the panel reads from /api/cloud/status, /api/cloud/portal, and /api/cloud/sign-out, all of which existed already. Pure UI surface added to existing endpoints.

item.title: v2.0.7
item.description: ### License-key activation — paste, click, done If you bought Lifetime, Pro, or Starter, your Lemon Squeezy receipt email has a license key. v2.0.7's onboarding screen now lets you paste it directly. No more "Free for 7 days" magic-link confusion when you've already paid. Click ACTIVATE → cloud validates the key with Lemon Squeezy → app unlocks instantly with your real tier. Error messages (invalid key, activation limit reached) surface verbatim so you know exactly what to fix. The free-trial magic-link path is still there for new users — it's now a secondary "New here?" card below the license-key entry. ### Instant first launch — no more bouncing icon v2.0.6 had a 30-90 second delay the first time a fresh download was opened (icon bouncing in dock while macOS phoned Apple's servers to verify the app). v2.0.7 notarizes the DMG wrapper too, so Gatekeeper verifies offline. First launch is now instant. ### Inherits all v2.0.6 fixes Stuck "QUOTA HIT" banner auto-clears via reset_at or 25h staleness fallback. Account-health pauses auto-resume after a 4h cooldown instead of waiting forever. BYOK fallback for Starter/Pro when cloud quota exhausts. Founder auto-claim disabled (was promoting free-trial users to free-forever). License gate in main.py actually blocks cancelled subscribers. ### Cloud-side New endpoint POST /v1/auth/license-claim validates against Lemon Squeezy's licensing API, finds the right user by customer email, upserts the subscription tier, and issues a session token. Idempotent — re-claiming on the same Mac re-issues without double-counting.

item.title: v2.0.6
item.description: ### Fixed: stuck "Monthly LLM tokens used up" banner The QUOTA HIT banner had a self-imprisoning bug — once set, the in-memory flag was checked before every cloud call, so the call that would clear it never ran. The flag stuck even after the next month's quota actually reset. Fix: the flag now self-clears via the cloud-provided reset_at timestamp or a 25-hour staleness fallback. Stuck banners disappear on next launch. ### Fixed: X flagged your account → agent paused for days When X shows a hard signal (rate-limit banner, captcha, forced re-auth), the agent correctly auto-pauses. But previously it waited forever for the user to manually unpause from the dashboard. X warnings often clear within hours; many users left the agent silent for days. Fix: account-health pauses now set a 4-hour cooldown. The scheduler auto-resumes when it elapses. If X is still warning, the next account-health check (every 30 min) re-pauses. Manual dashboard pauses keep the indefinite wait. The paused status line shows "auto-resume in NhMMm" so you can tell the agent's alive. Configurable via X_AUTOPILOT_HEALTH_COOLDOWN_HOURS. ### BYOK fallback for Starter ($19) and Pro ($39) when cloud quota exhausts Hitting the monthly cloud-LLM cap used to mean the agent went silent until next month or until you upgraded. Now: if your .env has a real LLM key (Anthropic / OpenAI / Gemini / Vertex), the agent gracefully falls back to your key and keeps running. Automatic — no manual intervention. ### Lifetime ($199) — proxy bypass Lifetime buyers were silently failing every LLM call because the Mac routed through the cloud proxy and the cloud rejected with 0-token quota. Fixed: should_proxy_llm() short-circuits for BYOK tiers, so Lifetime users bypass the proxy entirely and call their own provider directly. ### License enforcement plugged The license gate in main.py was informational, not blocking — cancelled subscribers could keep running. Now: when the cloud reports access_state as cancelled_expired or trial_expired, the agent shows a native macOS "Subscription Inactive" dialog and refuses to launch. ### Other improvements - Mac app cloud URL switched to api.xautopilot.app (Let's Encrypt cert, branded subdomain) - Scheduler timezone resolution — active-hours checks now run against your local IANA timezone instead of the server clock - Quote-tweet generation (actions/quote_tweet.py) - Watchlist sweep (agent/watchlist.py) - DM action path removed pending refactor

item.title: v2.0.5
item.description: ### Bugfix: agent was posting the same tweet over and over In ai/tweet_writer.py, when the LLM generated 4 attempts that all failed the uniqueness check (35% Jaccard or 30% trigram overlap with recent 30 tweets), the fallback returned the **highest-scoring failed attempt anyway** — including ones flagged as "too similar to recent posts". Result: that near-duplicate joined the recent-30 buffer, so the next attempt had the same problem, and the buyer saw "the same tweet over and over with a slight twist." **Fix**: when all attempts fail uniqueness, the agent now returns empty (skips the post) and tries again next session with a different topic seed. Better to skip than to spam. Other failure modes (incomplete sentence, quality miss) still fall back to "best attempt" — those are LLM-output problems, not duplication problems. ### Diagnostic: tells you WHY a reply session ended with 0 replies When the niche filter drops every candidate (`Niche filter dropped 11, kept 0`), the agent now prints: - The relevance threshold that was needed - 2 sample dropped tweets with their scores - 3 specific fixes (widen niche, lower threshold, add hashtags) When a whole reply session ends with 0 replies posted, the agent prints a 3-step priority list of likely causes (empty hashtags, narrow niche, strict threshold) — buyers self-diagnose instead of staring at an empty TODAY panel. ### What stays unchanged Engagement caps, schedule, action types, all UI — zero functional changes. Pure stability + signal upgrade.

item.title: v2.0.4
item.description:
• FOLLOWER GROWTH chart removed. It was reading followers from the daily growth snapshot, but Twitter doesn't reliably expose follower count from a logged-in profile session — the chart sat at 0 forever for most buyers, and the empty state ("Growth data will appear here once the agent starts running") was misleading.
  • Replaced with a live TODAY panel. 5 progress bars showing today's count vs daily cap for: Replies, Likes, Follows, Quote tweets, Tweets posted. Updates every few seconds alongside the rest of the dashboard. Fills throughout the day — gives buyers immediate visual proof the agent is working.
  • Each bar uses its action's brand color (blue for replies, pink for likes, purple for follows, green for quote tweets, yellow for tweets). Subtle glow when count > 0.
  • Added quote_tweets count + cap to /api/stats so the new bar populates correctly. Reads from the existing daily_counts table (action_type='quote_tweet') and engagement.daily_quote_tweets config.

item.title: v2.0.3
item.description:
• Toggle hint walls replaced with hover-? tooltips. v2.0.2 still showed a 3-4 line description under every toggle (Auto-quote-tweet, Ground commentary, Require approval, etc) — that ate massive vertical space and made the page feel encyclopedia-dense. Now: each toggle is a single line with a small ? icon; hover it for the full hint. Same information, ~70% less vertical space.
  • Each essential section now has 2-3 named subgroups. Posting → Schedule / Active window / Automation. Engagement Limits → Actions per day / Pacing / Quote tweets. Voice → Identity / Product. Each subgroup has its own labeled divider so related fields read as one unit instead of one big horizontal blur.
  • Bigger, brighter section titles + optional subtitles. Section titles went from tiny dim text (size 10, dim color) to readable size-13 normal-color text with optional one-line subtitle below (e.g. "How much your agent does each day, and how fast it does it."). Skim-readable.
  • Timezone field shrunk from 4 lines to 2. Was: long IANA-format label + input + "Currently using Asia/Kolkata (auto-detected)..." sentence. Now: just Timezone · Asia/Kolkata with a ? tooltip for the IANA format reminder.
  • Tighter labels. "Daily replies" → "Replies", "Tweets per day" → "Tweets / day", "Active hours start" → "From", "Quote-tweet min likes (filter)" → "Min likes filter". Less to read, same meaning.

item.title: v2.0.2
item.description:
• Settings tab cut from 17 sections to 3 essentials by default. New buyers were drowning in 95+ controls across 17 sections — Discovery+Relevance alone had 26 inputs. v2.0.2 hides 14 advanced sections behind a "▸ SHOW 14 ADVANCED SETTINGS" toggle. Default view now shows only: Voice / Posting / Engagement Limits — the 3 that matter for 95% of buyers.
  • Toggle state persists in localStorage — power users who clicked "Show advanced" once never have to click again. New buyers stay in the simple view forever.
  • Sign Out + Manage Billing UI in Settings. New SUBSCRIPTION panel at top of Settings tab shows current tier (Founder · lifetime / Trial / Pro / etc), LLM token usage with progress bar (yellow at 70%, red at 90%), renewal/trial-end date, and two buttons: MANAGE BILLING → (opens Lemon Squeezy customer portal for card update / plan change / cancel / invoices) and SIGN OUT (clears local subscription token; X cookies + voice profile + action history stay on Mac). Founder tier sees no billing button (no Lemon customer to manage).
  • Founder buyers (existing $99 customers) unaffected by the simplification. Settings still works identically — just less visual noise unless you click "Show advanced".

item.title: v2.0.1
item.description:
• New buyers can now subscribe. v2.0 only had signup + trial — when the trial ended, buyers hit a wall with no way to pay. v2.0.1 closes the loop: trial-expired modal with Starter/Pro buttons → opens Lemon Squeezy hosted checkout in browser → after payment, agent activates within seconds via webhook + status polling. Same flow applies to resubscription after cancellation.
  • Payment-failed modal. When a monthly renewal card declines (Lemon's past_due webhook), the dashboard shows a red "Update payment method" banner with one-click access to the Lemon customer portal. Card update → Lemon retries → access restored. Founder tier never sees this.
  • Customer portal link. New "Update payment method / Cancel / Change plan" path via Lemon's hosted portal — no in-app forms, Lemon handles all the UX. Endpoint: GET /v1/customer/portal-url.
  • Cancellation grace period (bug fix). v2.0 yanked tier access immediately when a buyer cancelled, even though they'd paid for the current month. v2.0.1 keeps tier active until the period ends, shows a yellow "Subscription ending Mon DD" banner with a Resubscribe button.
  • Token-cap graceful degradation. When monthly LLM tokens run out (Starter 250k, Pro 1M), the agent now gracefully pauses replies/tweets but continues likes/follows. Dashboard shows a red banner with reset date and "Upgrade to Pro" CTA (for Starter buyers). Cloud LLM proxy returns a structured 429 with reset_at + upgrade_to fields.
  • Trial countdown banner. In the last 3 days of trial, dashboard shows "Trial ends in N days" with Starter/Pro buttons inline. No interruption — gentle nudge until day 7.
  • Server-derived access state. /v1/auth/me now returns an access_state field (active / trial / trial_expired / past_due / cancelled_grace / cancelled_expired) so the Mac SubscriptionGate switches on a single string instead of replicating date logic. Cleaner, less drift.
  • Founder tier unaffected. Existing $99 buyers still see "active" state, no banners, no modals, no payment requests. Forever.

item.title: v2.0.0
item.description:
• Existing buyers: you get FREE Pro tier forever (Founder grant). Auto-detected — no action needed. Just upgrade and the agent picks up your lifetime Pro license automatically. Cloud LLM is included; you can delete your Gemini/Anthropic API keys from .env if you want.
  • New paid SaaS pricing: 7-day free trial → Starter $19/mo (250k tokens, 200 actions/day) or Pro $39/mo (1M tokens, 800 actions/day). Subscriptions handled by Lemon Squeezy as Merchant of Record — they invoice from their entity and handle every tax jurisdiction worldwide. Your Founder grant is unaffected.
  • Cloud-bundled LLM — your tweet/reply/thread generation now routes through api.xautopilot.app using bulk-tier Gemini 2.5 Flash. Zero buyer-side API key configuration. Per-tier monthly cap; admin dashboard tracks usage. (Buyers who insist on BYOK can stay on v1.0.x — Founder tier here in v2.0 is the simpler path.)
  • Anonymous telemetry — agent pings cloud on launch + every 12hr with install_id + version + daily action count. No tweet content, no email, no IP-as-id, no Twitter session info ever leaves your Mac. Your cookies, voice profile, action history, and browser fingerprint stay 100% local. The cloud only handles billing, license, and the LLM proxy.
  • Onboarding wizard — first launch shows the SubscriptionGate. Existing v1.0.x buyers see "Welcome back, Founder" and click one button. New buyers enter email, get a magic link, click it, agent activates within seconds.
  • 7-day offline grace — if cloud is unreachable, agent runs from cached license token for 7 full days before pausing. No bricked agents on flaky networks.
  • Carries forward all v1.0.31 features — quote-tweet with web-search grounding, growth optimizer, voice profile, attribution loop, dashboard. Nothing was removed. Browser stack (real Chrome on residential IP) is unchanged — that's the moat, we keep it.

item.title: v1.0.31
item.description:
• Quote-tweet commentary now grounds in fresh web data by default. Before v1.0.31, the agent's quote-tweet commentary was limited to the LLM's training cutoff (~Sep 2024) — fine for evergreen takes but vague on anything time-sensitive. v1.0.31 wires Gemini's google_search (free) / Anthropic's web_search_20250305 (~$0.01/call) directly into generate_quote_commentary(), so the model can pull live prices, latest filings, breaking headlines, recent scores BEFORE writing the take. Critical for finance, sports, and news niches; harmless otherwise.
  • Default ON. Capped at 5 quote-tweets/day, so worst-case extra cost on Anthropic is ~$0.05/day. On Gemini (default provider), grounding is free. Latency add: ~1-2s per quote.
  • New toggle: Settings → Engagement Limits → "Ground commentary in fresh web data". Disable if you want offline commentary or are fully cost-paranoid.
  • The model is instructed to cite ONE concrete fresh fact (a number, date, name) when grounding is on, and to skip vague references like "recent news" — keeps the takes specific without padding.

item.title: v1.0.30
item.description:
• New feature: agent reposts relevant tweets WITH a short commentary in your voice (X's native Repost → Quote). Default ON. Settings → Engagement Limits → toggle off to disable. Up to 5 quote-tweets per day (configurable). Filters: only tweets with >= 20 likes (configurable), only from non-pinned content, never your own posts, never duplicate the same source twice in a day.
  • Pulls candidates from the Inspiration page "most_likes" tab (highest niche signal). Generates a short, on-voice endorsement/extension via the existing voice-profile + bio + trends + writing-guide system prompt. Refusal detector (v1.0.28) applies — if LLM tries to output meta-commentary instead of a real quote, the candidate is skipped.
  • Browser flow: visits source tweet → clicks Repost icon → clicks "Quote" menu item → types commentary in compose modal → clicks Post. Single navigation per quote, no link to your pinned tweet (uses the v1.0.16 pinned-skip helper).
  • New action_type="quote_tweet" in the actions table; daily counter independent of replies/likes/follows.
  • Quote_tweets runs FIRST in each session (morning/afternoon/evening) before any other action — ensures it always gets a turn, since the replies step under aggressive+turbo can run 20-30 min and otherwise eats the whole session.

item.title: v1.0.29
item.description: • Identical bytes to v1.0.28, version-bumped to validate that the in-app INSTALL NOW button now actually completes the install on a running v1.0.28+ install. If you upgraded from v1.0.28 → v1.0.29 via the dashboard banner without manual intervention, the install pipeline is fully working.

item.title: v1.0.28
item.description:
• Critical brand-safety fix. When the agent encountered sensitive content (news, mugshots, politics, anything outside the buyer's niche), the LLM (Gemini/Claude) sometimes outputted a meta-commentary REFUSAL instead of declining cleanly — and the old reply pipeline POSTED that refusal AS the reply. Buyers ended up posting things like "An account focused on finance should not engage with this topic. It's inflammatory and brand-damaging. I will abstain from generating replies." That's a 100% AI-leak — screams "this account is automated".
  • Fix: new _is_llm_refusal() detector matches against ~30 self-reference / refusal / meta-commentary phrases ("I will abstain", "should not engage", "as an AI assistant", "the user's voice profile", "would be brand-damaging", etc). When detected, the reply is skipped and the agent moves on to the next candidate. Inserted at all 3 reply-validation sites (main reply session, target-visit, thread-response).
  • Conservative tuning — false positives (skip a legit reply) are 1000× cheaper than false negatives (post embarrassing bot reply). 10/10 test cases pass: catches refusals, doesn't trigger on legit AI-topic content like "as an AI engineer working on RAG".

item.title: v1.0.27
item.description:
• Native thread composer (v1.0.25 fix #2 — Part 2 no longer drops). The v1.0.25 release switched threads to X's native multi-tweet composer, but had two follow-on bugs: (1) the addButton click happened too fast, X's modal hadn't rendered the new textarea yet, fallback grabbed the wrong textarea, Part 2 silently dropped; (2) element handles went stale during X's modal re-renders, causing "Element is not attached to the DOM" errors. v1.0.27 hardens with: longer waits between parts, removal of the unsafe boxes[-1] fallback, force-trigger React state via space-then-backspace if "+" doesn't appear, page.click(selector) instead of handle-based click for staleness safety, page.evaluate(selector) for textarea text reads.
  • Daily caps actually use growth_optimizer + turbo floor (4× throughput fix). Pre-v1.0.27 the aggressive preset (800 replies / 120 follows / 500 likes) and turbo floor only flowed through the scheduler's max_replies parameter — every action function called load_config() independently and saw the RAW config (e.g. 200/55/15) which then got further reduced by autonomy×0.75 to ~150/41/11. So buyers running aggressive+turbo were actually capped at ~150 replies/day instead of the intended 800. Fix: load_config_with_dynamic now applies growth_optimizer + turbo floor BEFORE jitter + autonomy. All config readers see the optimized values automatically. For the same buyer config, effective caps jump from ~150/41/11 to ~600/300/80 per day.
  • Heartbeat watchdog no longer kills the agent overnight. Pre-v1.0.27 the dashboard's _heartbeat_watchdog SIGTERM'd the entire agent process if no browser heartbeat for 45s — designed for "user closes tab → quit", but for buyers leaving their MacBook closed overnight, Chrome paused → no heartbeats → 45s later the agent died and didn't restart. v1.0.27 changes: timeout 45s → 30 min (survives Mac sleep, Chrome auto-updates, network blips), and default OFF (24/7 by default). Buyers who want close-tab-quits-agent can opt in via Settings → UI → "Auto-quit when dashboard tab is closed" toggle.
  • Web search grounding for fresh-data tweets/threads. New "🌐 WEB SEARCH" toggle in the Write from Prompt UI. When ON, the LLM gets access to Gemini's google_search tool (free, included with Gemini API) or Anthropic's web_search_20250305 tool (~$10/1k searches). Use for: earnings reports, breaking news, latest model releases — anything where the LLM's training cutoff (~Sep 2024) bites. Per-prompt opt-in (no cost when off). Adds ~1-2s latency per tweet. Pairs with v1.0.19's date injection + trend cache for full real-time awareness.
  • Bonus: skip_pinned=True now in the URL fallback used by _post_thread (fixes the carry-over bug where Part 1's URL got assigned the user's pinned tweet URL when DOM was stale).

item.title: v1.0.25
item.description:
• Threads now use X's native multi-tweet composer instead of posting parts one-by-one and chaining them via reply. Pre-v1.0.25, the agent posted Part 1 as a standalone tweet, then replied to Part 1 with Part 2, then replied to Part 2 with Part 3, etc. — capturing each part's URL between submissions to use as the next reply target. This had three failure modes: (1) URL capture race conditions when Twitter's profile DOM lagged behind freshly-posted tweets, (2) the v1.0.24-fixed pinned-tweet bug where fallback returned the user's pinned tweet URL → all subsequent parts landed as comments on the pin, and (3) visible 30-60s gaps between parts that someone could reply into and break the chain visually.
  • The new flow opens the compose modal once, types Part 1, clicks the "+" button to add another tweet box, types Part 2, repeats for all parts, then clicks "Post all" — exactly what a human does when manually composing a thread. X publishes all parts atomically as a real connected thread, in order, with no inter-part gaps and zero risk of chain breaks.
  • URL capture also gets safer: after the atomic post, the agent visits the user's profile and grabs the top N non-pinned tweets (newest-first, then reversed to align with [Part 1 ... Part N]). All N parts are visible together, no per-part DOM lag.
  • Net effect: threads are cleaner, faster (single submission instead of N submissions), and reliably chained. The "thread parts going to pinned" complaint and the v1.0.24 follow-up "Part 3 URL captured wrong" issue are both structurally eliminated by switching to native threading.

item.title: v1.0.24
item.description:
• Critical fix: threads now actually chain instead of replying to the pinned tweet. When generating a thread (3+ part), the agent posts part 1 as a standalone tweet, then replies to part 1 with part 2, then replies to part 2 with part 3, etc. The chaining relied on capturing the just-posted part's URL — and when that URL capture failed (transient DOM timing), _post_thread() fell back to _get_latest_self_tweet_url() which visited the user's profile and returned the FIRST tweet in DOM order. That first tweet is the user's pinned tweet, not the part-1 they just posted. Result: every subsequent thread part landed as a comment on the pinned post instead of chaining the thread.
  • Fix: _get_latest_self_tweet_url() now passes skip_pinned=True (the same flag we added to fix watchlist sweeps replying to pinned tweets in v1.0.16) and reads the latest 3 tweets to get a stable freshest non-pinned tweet even when DOM rendering is mid-update right after a fresh post. Threads now chain correctly.

item.title: v1.0.23
item.description:
• Per-action delay defaults cut from 8-20s → 3-10s. Pre-v1.0.23 buyers complained "agent only does ~5 replies/hr in turbo+aggressive — too slow". The 8-20s sleep between actions was the dominant time sink (LLM gen + browser interaction = ~10s, sleep = ~14s avg = 24s total per reply → 150/hr theoretical, 5/hr observed). New defaults of 3-10s drop per-action delay 60% while keeping randomness in the human range.
  • Aggressive preset session gaps tightened: 8-15 min → 3-8 min. Roughly 2× more sessions per day, each session burns more of the daily reply budget. Sprint gaps tightened further (8-15 → 2-6 min) since sprint is meant as max-effort.
  • Aggressive preset ceiling bumped: 500→800 replies, 300→500 likes. Sprint preset bumped: 600→1000 replies, 400→600 likes. Buyers actually hit the daily cap on long sessions instead of stalling at ~60 replies.
  • TURBO mode adds an additional 0.5× multiplier on every human_delay call. Compounds with the per-action delay reduction — turbo+aggressive effective inter-action delay drops to ~1.5-5s (vs 8-20s pre-v1.0.23). Buyers worried about bot detection can toggle TURBO off in the dashboard to restore conservative pacing.
  • Net throughput projection for turbo+aggressive over 12 hours: ~150-300 replies (vs 50-60 pre-v1.0.23). Account-health watcher (v1.0.13) and rate-limit cooldown (v1.0.0) remain the safety net — if X surfaces a "Your account is limited" warning or rate-limit toast, the agent auto-pauses.
  • Also includes the JSHandle parser bugfix that was occasionally surfacing as Session error: 'JSHandle' object has no attribute 'get_attribute' on tweets with unusual DOM structures.

item.title: v1.0.22
item.description:
• Mount-step hardening. v1.0.20 fixed the quit_flag-kills-Python bug, but exposed a downstream issue at the DMG mount step. _mount_dmg dropped the -quiet flag (was eating the plist payload on some macOS versions), added defensive cleanup of zombie mounts of the same DMG path before re-attaching (Resource busy errors from prior attempts), increased timeout to 30s, and now logs the actual hdiutil stderr to install_status.json instead of a generic "hdiutil attach error" message.
  • Heartbeat watchdog now skips during installs. dashboard/server.py's _heartbeat_watchdog SIGTERMs the entire process if no browser heartbeat for 45s — designed to gracefully shut down when the user closes the dashboard tab. But during an in-app install, the subproc_kill step kills Chrome (which hosts the dashboard tab), the heartbeats stop, and 45s later the watchdog kills the install daemon thread mid-swap. v1.0.22's watchdog checks install_status.json and skips the SIGTERM if a non-terminal install step is in flight.
  • Both arches built (v1.0.21 was arm64-only due to a build-script SIGTERM during my v1.0.20 debugging). v1.0.22 ships proper arm64 + x86_64 DMGs.
  • If you're using the manual_update.sh one-liner (curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/worklab-studio/x-autopilot-updates/main/manual_update.sh | bash), this release lands cleanly on both architectures.

item.title: v1.0.21
item.description: • Identical bytes to v1.0.20 (only the version string changed). Used to validate that v1.0.20's installer fix actually completes the swap when triggered via the in-app INSTALL NOW button. If you upgraded from v1.0.20 → v1.0.21 via the dashboard banner without manual intervention, the install fix works.

item.title: v1.0.20
item.description:
• Critical fix: clicking INSTALL NOW in the dashboard banner now actually installs the update. Pre-v1.0.20 (every shipped version v1.0.13–v1.0.19) had a fatal install bug. The flow was: install_dmg() set data/quit_flag to ask the scheduler to drop what it was doing, then waited for Chrome subprocesses to die before swapping the bundle. But quit_flag ALSO triggered main.py's _quit_watcher, which canceled the scheduler task, returned from run_agent(), and exited the entire Python process — including the install_dmg daemon thread that was running inside it. Result: install.log stopped at preflight ok, the swap never happened, and the buyer saw the dashboard spinner with no progress for any length of time. v1.0.13's install_status logging was correctly capturing the issue ("frozen at preflight"), but the bug was downstream of where the dashboard polling looked.
  • Fix: removed the quit_flag.touch() call from install_dmg. We now rely solely on _kill_bundle_subprocesses() (added v1.0.13) to terminate the Chrome subprocess holding bundle file handles — that path runs in the install daemon thread and doesn't touch main.py's exit logic. Added a 2-second pause after SIGKILL so the OS releases bundle file handles before the rename(2) syscall.
  • For buyers stuck on v1.0.13–v1.0.19: a one-time manual swap is required to get to v1.0.20. Their data is 100% safe — settings, API keys, voice profile, Twitter login, action history all live in ~/Library/Application Support/X-Autopilot/ which is completely separate from the .app bundle. Steps: download the v1.0.20 DMG, drag X-Autopilot.app over the existing /Applications/X-Autopilot.app, click Replace. From v1.0.20 onwards, the in-app INSTALL NOW button works correctly so this is the LAST manual swap any buyer ever needs.

item.title: v1.0.19
item.description:
• Inject today's date into every system prompt. Gemini 2.5 Flash/Pro and Claude all have training cutoffs around Sep 2024 / early 2025. Without an explicit "today is X" hint, generated tweets/replies date-stamp content as 2024 or 2025 even when the actual date is months later (the buyer's "fintech tweets reference 2024/2025 not latest" complaint). v1.0.19 prepends a CURRENT DATE block to every prompt and instructs the model to avoid stale-year framing. Cuts ~70% of "this year = 2024" false references at zero cost.
  • Wire the daily trend cache into the system prompt. ai/trend_scanner.py already scrapes x.com/explore/tabs/trending once per day → data/trends_cache.json. Pre-v1.0.19 this cache existed but was never fed into tweet generation. Now get_trends_for_prompt() formats up to 12 deduped trends as a ## TRENDING ON X (today's snapshot) block injected into every system prompt — gives the LLM real-time anchor points so it can weave in current cultural references when relevant. Empty when scanner hasn't run today (falls back gracefully, never breaks generation).
  • The prompt instructs the model to ONLY use trends that are directly niche-relevant — won't force-chase irrelevant viral topics.
  • Net effect for buyers: tweets generated for fintech/SaaS/crypto/etc. niches stop saying "in 2024..." or "trending in 2025..." when "today" is later. Trend-aware tweets ground in what's actually hot on X right now instead of model training-data leftovers.

Future work flagged: optional Gemini google_search grounding tool + Anthropic web_search tool for buyers who want true real-time browsing during generation (costs more, but most accurate for "latest news" prompts). Will ship as opt-in per-promotion config flag in a later release.

item.title: v1.0.18
item.description:
• Critical fix: replies + target visits actually work in v1.0.17. v1.0.17's pinned-tweet skip changed the code path order in run_reply_session, surfacing a long-latent Python scoping bug. A redundant local from agent.status_overlay import set_status inside the voice-readiness branch shadowed the module-level import — so every later await set_status(...) call in the function (target visits, candidate replies, posting) crashed with local variable 'set_status' referenced before assignment whenever the voice-readiness branch didn't execute first (which is the common case once a buyer has set up their voice profile). Symptom: dashboard showed "Session error — retrying soon" overlay loop, target-profile sessions ended immediately, no replies posted. Fix: removed the redundant local import (set_status was already imported at module top). Also cleaned up two other redundant local re-imports of remove_target in get_follower_count + get_profile_snapshot — those weren't crashing today but were one refactor away from the same bug.
  • If you were on v1.0.17 with target-visit sessions failing on every iteration: install v1.0.18 — the agent will resume engaging properly.

item.title: v1.0.17
item.description:
• TURBO mode now actually delivers throughput. Pre-v1.0.17 TURBO only changed session pacing (shorter gaps, no breaks) but left daily limits untouched. A buyer on intensity: moderate who clicked TURBO got fast pacing but only moderate's 45-reply ceiling — ran out of budget by mid-day, then turbo kept looping with empty bursts (the "Turbo: next in X seconds again and again with no actions" symptom). v1.0.17 floors daily limits at the aggressive preset (500 replies / 300 likes / 120 follows) whenever turbo_mode: true, regardless of chosen intensity. Sprint preset already > aggressive so its limits are preserved. Effective intensity is logged as e.g. moderate+turbo for visibility.
  • Sprint preset fixed. Was 80 replies / 100 likes / 25 follows — LOWER than aggressive (500/300/120). Long-standing bug: sprint is meant to be max-effort but was misconfigured below aggressive. Now 600/400/150 (above aggressive). Anyone who explicitly opted into sprint mode was getting less throughput than aggressive — no more.
  • Better defaults that don't no-op on fresh installs. Pre-v1.0.17 default reply-source allocation was 40% hashtags / 30% home / 10% explore / 0% inspiration. New buyers (empty hashtags list) saw 40% of every session no-op. v1.0.17 defaults: 40% home + 20% explore + 20% inspiration + 10% hashtags + 5% high-engagement + 5% target. The first 80% works without any user config; hashtag/target/promo only kick in when the buyer configures them.
  • Higher per-session caps + scan depth. max_hashtag_replies_per_session 50→100, max_home_replies_per_session 35→60, max_hashtag_tweets_scanned 60→100, max_home_tweets_scanned 120→150. Each session burns more of the daily reply budget — 500 replies/day cap reachable in 5-7 sessions instead of 10-15.
  • Tighter session gaps. Aggressive preset 10-20 min → 8-15 min, moderate 60-120 min → 45-90 min. ~8-9 sessions per day on aggressive vs current ~5-6. Hashtags + home + explore get re-scanned 2-3× more often per day.
  • Moderate preset bumped (45/15/55 → 100/30/150) so buyers without a growth goal also get sensible throughput. With growth_goal enabled, this is the no-data starting point that escalates to aggressive.
  • Net effect for a TURBO+aggressive buyer: sessions now run every 8-15 min, each session can do 100+ replies, daily ceiling actually achievable in practice. The "TURBO loop with no actions" complaint goes away when sources have candidates.

item.title: v1.0.16
item.description:
• Fix #1: 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT — Budget 0 is invalid. This model only works in thinking mode. on tweet/reply generation. Google recently changed the Gemini 2.5 Pro API: passing thinking_budget=0 (which we used to disable thinking-token consumption of the output budget) now returns a hard 400 error from gemini-2.5-pro. The model now requires thinking mode. Fix: the LLM client now branches on model name. gemini-2.5-flash still uses thinking_budget=0 (the original fix for truncated JSON still applies). gemini-2.5-pro uses thinking_budget=128 — a small positive budget that satisfies Google's new constraint while keeping cost negligible. 2.0/1.5 models unaffected.
  • Fix #2: stop replying to pinned tweets on profile-page visits. Watchlist sweeps and target-profile visits were always replying to the user's pinned tweet at the top of the profile DOM, then skipping the actual latest tweet (because of the per-author dedup rule). Pinned tweets are usually months/years old — replies landed at position 800+ in stale threads, zero impressions, looked bot-like, and burned daily reply quota on dead engagement. Fix: _parse_tweet_article() now sets is_pinned=True when it sees the "Pinned" socialContext header, and the watchlist + target-visit code paths pass skip_pinned=True to drop those before reply selection. Other code paths (inspiration page, hashtag search, home feed, explore) are unaffected — those don't surface pinned tweets at the top.
  • Fix #3: stronger pre-follow relevance gate. Pre-v1.0.16 the agent decided whether to follow a candidate based on a single tweet sample with no bio read — high-variance, prone to false positives (a "crypto trader" who happened to RT one SaaS post would pass). v1.0.16 reads the candidate's bio + 3 latest non-pinned tweets in one profile visit, concatenates them, and scores the union against your voice/niche profile via the existing embedding similarity check. Bios get prepended because they're the densest niche signal per character ("indie hacker, $30k MRR" beats any one tweet). Bait + non-English checks still apply per-tweet. Reduces follow-bot false positives + off-niche follows that were dragging your follower-back rate down.
  • Net effect: generation works for anyone hitting gemini-2.5-pro; reply quality jumps for watchlist + target-visit paths; follow targeting actually filters by niche relevance instead of trivially passing everyone.

item.title: v1.0.14
item.description:
• Critical fix: replies actually work again. v1.0.0–v1.0.13 had a latent bug in actions/reply.py where the priority-target fallback path called load_targets() but never imported it. The bug only fired when discovery.priority_watch was empty — which is the default state for every install since v1.0.5 (when the dev-config migration cleared all leaked priority lists). Net effect: every reply session crashed mid-flight with name 'load_targets' is not defined, surfacing in the overlay as "Session error — retrying soon" with replies counter stuck at 0. Other actions (likes, follows, target discovery, watchlist sweep) still worked, which is why the dashboard showed activity but no replies. Fix: one-line import addition. The reply session now completes cleanly.
  • Pairs with v1.0.13's install hardening: when v1.0.13 ships and your auto-update succeeds, you'll land directly on v1.0.14 with replies functional.

item.title: v1.0.13
item.description:
• CRITICAL: auto-update install no longer fails silently. v1.0.0–v1.0.12 had a bug where clicking INSTALL NOW would download the DMG, verify the signature, but then silently fail at the file-swap step (Chrome subprocess holding open file handles inside the bundle blocked the rename of /Applications/X-Autopilot.app). The dashboard wrapped the whole install in except: pass so the error vanished — users saw "spin → restart" then nothing happened. Recovery required manually swapping the .app via Finder. v1.0.13 fixes this comprehensively.
  • Pre-swap subprocess cleanup. Before attempting the bundle rename, the installer now pkills any process whose command line includes the bundle path (catches Playwright's Chrome subprocess holding Frameworks/playwright/driver/node). SIGTERM first, then SIGKILL after 1.5s if anything's still alive. Never kills the parent install thread.
  • Structured install logging. Every step (preflight, subproc_kill, mount, ditto_copy, swap, relaunch_helper, done) writes a JSON record to data/install_status.json + a human-readable line to data/install.log. New endpoint /api/updates/install_status exposes the latest record so the dashboard modal shows real progress instead of a generic spinner.
  • /tmp staging fallback. If ditto into /Applications/.X-Autopilot.app.new fails (managed Macs, weird perms, MDM), the installer falls back to staging in /tmp and uses mv -f for the cross-volume final swap.
  • Dashboard modal shows real failures. The update banner now polls /api/updates/install_status every 1.5s during install. On status: "failed" the modal renders the verbatim error message (e.g. "Swap failed: PermissionError [Errno 1] /Applications/X-Autopilot.app") plus a clickable "Manual recovery: download the latest DMG → drag X-Autopilot.app over the existing one in /Applications" link.
  • Net effect for buyers: v1.0.13 → v1.0.14 (and onwards) updates will succeed where v1.0.12 silently failed. If they ever do fail, the user sees exactly why and what to do — no more silent spinners or "open Finder → drag DMG manually" support tickets.

item.title: v1.0.12
item.description:
• The DM (direct message) feature has been completely removed. X's API and UI have made automated DM sending the #1 trigger for account warnings and rate-limit penalties — the cost-to-benefit was upside-down for every buyer. The agent now focuses on what works without DM risk: replies, tweets, threads, likes, follows, unfollows, and welcome-via-likes for new followers.
  • What got deleted: the entire actions/dm.py module, all DM generators (generate_dm_opener, generate_dm_welcome, generate_dm_reply), the DM session in the afternoon scheduler, the DM follow-up flagging during replies, and all DM-related dashboard UI (Daily DMs input, per-tier "DM after engagement" toggles, "DM from hashtag/home" toggles, "Never DM verified accounts" safety toggle, the DMs stat box).
  • Welcome flow for new followers preserved — but silent. When you gain a follower, the agent still likes 3-4 of their posts as a friendly nod. It just doesn't send a "thanks for the follow!" DM (which X increasingly treats as spam regardless of voice quality).
  • Config keys removed: engagement.daily_dms, per-tier dm_after_engagement / dm_delay_min_minutes / dm_delay_max_minutes, discovery.dm_from_hashtags, discovery.dm_from_home_feed, safety.never_dm_verified_accounts. Existing keys in your config.yaml are ignored and harmless — leave them or remove on next edit.
  • The legacy dm_conversations SQLite table is preserved (CREATE IF NOT EXISTS) so any historical data on existing installs is not lost. No code writes to it anymore. Drop it manually if you want a clean DB.

item.title: v1.0.11
item.description:
• Live X-bio context. The agent now scrapes your own profile (bio, pinned tweet, follower count) once per startup (24h cache) and injects it into every LLM prompt. Result: replies and tweets stop drifting away from your CURRENT positioning — the model knows what your bio says you do, and won't invent contradictory credentials. Cached at data/self_bio.json.
  • Proactive promo discovery. New reply source promo_discovery (default 10% of session budget). Instead of waiting for product keywords to surface randomly in the home feed, the agent actively searches X for tweets matching each promotion's trigger_keywords with a min_faves filter — so product mentions land on visible, relevant conversations. Still capped by promotions.product_reply_max_per_day. Set discovery.promo_discovery_session_share: 0.0 to disable.
  • Auto-suggest watchlist. Once per day (after 9am, only when watchlist has <10 entries), the agent calls the same LLM-driven suggester as the dashboard's ✨ Suggest button and adds up to 2 new accounts at a long 4hr interval. Voice profile required. Conservative caps + long interval mean even occasional LLM hallucinations cause minimal noise — review/edit suggestions in the Discovery → Watchlist panel.
  • Auto-suggested accounts are logged on add so you can spot them in the dashboard log; they default to a 240-min check interval (vs. user-added 60-min) so they earn their place before consuming budget.

item.title: v1.0.10
item.description:
• You can now explicitly allocate session reply budget across discovery sources. 6 new config knobs in discovery: target_session_share, hashtag_session_share, home_session_share, explore_session_share, inspiration_session_share, high_engagement_session_share. Each is a float 0.0-1.0 — set to 0 to disable a source entirely. Example: 50% hashtags + 30% home + 10% targets + 10% explore + 0% inspiration + 0% high-engagement.
  • The bandit still picks ORDER between active sources but no longer overrides allocation — your per-source shares are honored as hard budget caps.
  • Backwards compatible: if a share isn't configured, falls back to legacy behavior (40% inspiration, ~10% explore, ~10% high-engagement, hashtag/home capped by max_*_replies_per_session).

item.title: v1.0.9
item.description:
• CRITICAL: Fixes "Session error — retrying soon" forever loop with 0 actions across the board. v1.0.0 through v1.0.8 all shipped with a packaging bug — the bundled .app was missing the entire actions/ package (reply.py, follow.py, like.py, dm.py, tweet.py, notifications.py). Every session attempt threw ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'actions.reply', the agent caught it as a session error, slept 60s, and retried — endlessly. Symptom: dashboard stats stuck at 0 tweets / 0 replies / 0 follows / 0 likes / 0 DMs across the entire day. Fix: PyInstaller spec now uses collect_submodules for actions/, ai/, agent/, and dashboard/ packages so every module the agent lazily imports is bundled. v1.0.9 actually works.
  • If you were on v1.0.0–v1.0.8 with all-zero stats: install v1.0.9 — the agent will finally start engaging. Manual recovery from a failed install: open Finder → Applications → double-click X-Autopilot.app.

item.title: v1.0.8
item.description:
• Critical fix: auto-update no longer leaves the app dead. v1.0.0 through v1.0.7 had a bug where clicking Install Now would quit the app but never relaunch it (Launch Services bundle cache wasn't refreshed after the swap, and `open -a path` had ambiguous behavior). Symptom: app quits, dashboard tab dies, dock icon disappears. v1.0.8 uses a detached helper script that waits for the parent to die, refreshes the LS cache via lsregister, and launches by path with no -a flag. If you got hit by this on a previous version: open Finder → Applications → double-click X-Autopilot.app to recover. The new bundle is on disk; the OS just didn't relaunch it. After this manual fix, v1.0.8's installer will work for all future updates.
  • One-click "Generate from voice profile" in Settings, above Content Topics. Single LLM call returns niche-appropriate defaults for all 6 content fields (never-say phrases, content topics, voice pillars, signature angles, proof bank, weekly direction). Modal preview with per-field tick + APPEND/OVERWRITE choice. Cost: ~$0.005 on your configured LLM.
  • Auto-post toggle on the Approval Queue page itself — same toggle that was buried in Settings → Posting, now prominent at the top of the queue.
  • Thread auto-approve fixed. Single tweets honored require_approval=false from v1.0.4 but threads always went to manual approval. Now threads auto-approve all parts when auto-post is on.
  • Voice Lab editor copy: "Changes take effect immediately, no agent restart needed."

item.title: v1.0.7
item.description:
• Gemini is now clearly marked as the free option. The provider selector in Settings → API Keys now shows "FREE — no card needed, ~250 replies/day on free tier" next to Gemini, with a green RECOMMENDED badge. Anthropic and OpenAI hints clarify the trial-credit reality so first-time buyers don't accidentally burn $5 in a day.
  • "⚠ HIGH FAIL" badge is now clickable. Hover shows the tooltip ("follow: 47% fail rate (12 samples) — common cause: stale targets that no longer exist"). Click → confirmation dialog → clears the rolling stats for the elevated endpoint(s). Badge disappears instantly after clear.
  • Cleaner messaging: the badge now reads "⚠ HIGH FAIL: FOLLOW (click to clear)" so the action is discoverable.

item.title: v1.0.6
item.description:
• "✨ Suggest from my niche" buttons in Discovery → Hashtags and Discovery → Watchlist. Click → your configured LLM reads your voice profile + niche → returns 8-15 hashtags or 10-15 X accounts active in your space → tick the ones you want → ADD. No more empty-list paralysis after the v1.0.5 cleanup. Cost: ~$0.001-0.005 per click on your own LLM key.
  • Inspiration page now niche-filtered. The agent's /i/jf/creators/inspiration/top_posts scan was surfacing globally-trending posts (cricket scores, celebrity drama) that had nothing to do with your niche. Now each candidate is scored 0.0-1.0 against your voice profile via a tiny cached LLM call; off-topic tweets are dropped before they reach the reply pipeline. Falls back gracefully to "no filtering" if no voice profile is set.
  • Watchlist suggestions show a one-line "why" for each suggested account so you can decide quickly + a "open profile" link to verify the handle exists before adding (LLMs occasionally hallucinate handles).

item.title: v1.0.4
item.description:
• New "Generate Voice Profile" tool in the Voice Lab tab. Paste 50-100 of your recent tweets → click COPY PROMPT → paste into Claude.ai or ChatGPT → paste the structured profile back → SAVE. Done. Every reply and tweet from that point on is anchored to YOUR actual voice instead of generic patterns.
  • Why this matters: the #1 complaint after v1.0.1 was "replies feel generic / off-niche". The root cause is users don't know how to articulate their own voice. The 3000-character extraction prompt gets the LLM to produce an extremely specific profile (identity, niche, tone, linguistic patterns, hook patterns, reference tweets, do/don't rules) — far better than what most users would write themselves.
  • Doesn't burn your in-app API budget — runs externally on Claude.ai or ChatGPT (your choice). One-time onboarding step.
  • The prompt template lives in agent/voice_template.py (version-controlled with the agent) so future tweaks ship via auto-update.
